does_not_prove: that the resulting dreams are better, only that they differ and are grounded in the day
that the first-person stances are accurate about the day
longitudinal persona adaptation over many days
proves: two consecutive days produce different journals
the day's events reach the dream and are blended with persona memory rather than replacing it
the draw is by quota per stratum and is recorded in residue_links.json
a many-commit day compresses to at most 8 events

day_draw_note: an 11-commit day scores 1.0 on every code event and would take the entire day quota, silencing the affect signal. How the human felt is what makes this a dream about a person rather than a changelog.
method: ingest each day's events into /memory, then generate a dream per day and compare the resulting journal.md by sha256
read_path: AQL exact match on the day, not /recall. A day is an exact-match question. Note that /recall scope filtering was repaired upstream in graph-memory-operator#100 and now works; AQL remains correct for an exact date.
selection_note: top-k is not used. The recall queries are constants, so top-k over one pool returned the same documents every cycle -- which is why five consecutive dreams were byte-identical. A quota reserves room for today regardless of how today ranks, and reserves room for identity so a busy day cannot become the whole dream.
